In the one fly PARS2 precedent the engaged kinase was GCN2, with phospho-PERK unchanged, so a PERK-arm inhibitor would not be the matched tool there; which kinase, if any, is engaged in WWOX-deficient neural cells is unmeasured.

Whether the ISR in a WWOX-deficient system is compensatory rather than harmful: in the AFG3L2 precedent (PMID 37804316) DELE1 or HRI siRNA slows the growth of patient fibroblasts in low-glucose culture (neither was removed in mice), and a GADD34-targeted compound slightly improves patient-fibroblast growth in low-glucose culture and, given to the dams around birth and then daily to the pups, extends survival of the knockout mice (about 6 days at the median by plot reading, 5 treated knockouts or a multiple; the authors write 'only 10 days'; eIF2alpha phosphorylation and ATF4 not measured in treated mice), a different direction from the PARS2 fly, with different species, endpoint and manipulation; the AFG3L2 kinase evidence is siRNA in fibroblasts, GCN2 and PERK were not tested, and the compound's target is disputed: an in vitro study with purified PPP1R15A fragments found Sephin1 at the tested concentration without effect on complex association or dissociation (biolayer interferometry) and Sephin1 at escalating concentrations (top concentration not stated in the text or legend) without effect on eIF2alpha-P dephosphorylation, and guanabenz inert at the high concentration tested in the enzymatic assay (PMID 28447936, Figures 7 and 8; ADV-276, 2026-11-25); the authors limit the statement of no direct interference with complex assembly or stability to that experimental system.

A systemic bumetanide response therefore requires verification of relevant exposure, that is a free brain concentration in the NKCC1 range of about 1.5 to 2.5 micromolar; arithmetic from the mouse figures (brain unbound fraction 6 to 17 percent for three diuretics, brain to plasma ratio about 0.015 to 0.02) puts the corresponding total brain concentration at about 9 to 42 micromolar, an assumption-bound figure and not a prediction (the neonatal maturation of the barrier and efflux in the Wwox-null model is not addressed by these sources; the human plasma concentration is not stated in the US label excerpt read, so it is UNKNOWN here).
